author: Ari Koslow
title: Jose Cabrera to make MLB debut Sunday
desc: Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo said Jose Cabrera will start on Sunday against the Twins.
impact: Cabrera will be making his MLB debut. He has posted a 3.69 ERA over 12 starts across Double-A and Triple-A this season.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Kyle Schwarber slugs three home runs Saturday
desc: Kyle Schwarber went 4-for-5 with three home runs and six RBI in the Phillies 15-3 win over the Mets on Saturday.
impact: Schwarber hit two home runs off two different pitchers as part of an eight-run third inning for the Phillies. He later went deep again in the seventh inning. He now leads the league with 28 home runs.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Bryce Harper hits for cycle Saturday
desc: Bryce Harper went 4-for-5 with a home run and three RBI in the Phillies 15-3 win over the Mets on Saturday.
impact: Harper needed just five innings to hit for the cycle, going deep to open the scoring in the first inning before he doubled and singled in the third inning and hit a two-run triple in the fifth inning. It was the 11th cycle in Phillies franchise history.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Cristopher Sanchez earns win Saturday
desc: Cristopher Sanchez allowed one run on five hits over six innings with five strikeouts and one walk in a win on Saturday against the Mets.
impact: Sanchez didn't need to do much as he was given 10 runs of support by the Phillies lineup in the first three innings alone. He'll face the Nationals next.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Manny Machado hits go-ahead home run, drives in five Saturday
desc: Manny Machado went 2-for-5 with a home run and five RBI in the Padres 6-4 win over the Rangers on Saturday.
impact: Machado crushed a three-run home run in the 10th inning that wound up winning the game for San Diego. He previously opened the scoring with an RBI double in the third inning. He is slashing .178/.256/.367 with 13 home runs and 41 RBI on the season.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Mason Miller earns save Saturday
desc: Mason Miller earned his 20th save of the season on Saturday against the Rangers.
impact: Miller made his first appearance since being activated from the bereavement list. He entered the game in the 10th inning with a 6-3 lead, allowing the ghost runner on second base to score but recording two strikeouts to earn the save.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Walker Buehler strikes out seven Saturday
desc: Walker Buehler allowed one run on five hits over 5 1/3 innings with seven strikeouts and one walk in a no-decision on Saturday against the Rangers.
impact: Buehler had thrown five scoreless innings. He allowed back-to-back doubles in the sixth inning when he was removed from the game. He'll carry a 3.96 ERA into his next outing against the Dodgers.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Emerson Hancock takes loss Saturday
desc: Emerson Hancock allowed five runs on four hits over 5 1/3 innings with six strikeouts and two walks in a loss on Saturday against the Red Sox.
impact: Hancock has now allowed 11 runs over his past two starts after posting a 2.74 ERA across his first 13 starts of the season. He'll look to bounce back next time out against the Guardians.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Jackson Holliday (groin) exits early Saturday
desc: Jackson Holliday exited Saturday's game against the Dodgers because of groin tightness.
impact: Holliday will be further evaluated. He is day-to-day heading into Sunday.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Zack Gelof out of lineup Saturday due to not feeling well
desc: Zack Gelof was held out of Saturday's lineup because he didn't feel his best after arriving at the ballpark.
impact: Gelof was hit in the helmet by a pitch on Friday. He is day-to-day heading into Sunday.

author: David Leisering
title: Dylan Lee earns third victory of season Saturday
desc: Dylan Lee pitched around a two-out single in the top of the ninth and earned his third win of the season when Ozzie Albies hit a walk-off, two-run homer in the home half on Saturday in Atlanta's victory over Milwaukee.
impact: Lee improved to 3-0 on the season as he has turned himself into one of the best unheralded relievers in all of baseball. The lefthander has not been scored upon in his last nine outings and has allowed opponents to score in just four of his 35 appearances this season. Along with his 3-0 record, Lee has 15 holds, a 1.08 ERA, and a 0.66 WHIP, limiting opponents to a .147 average while posting a 42:5 K:BB ratio in 33.1 innings of work. It is not out of the question that Lee could be looking at an All-Star nod for the first time in his career. His numbers are certainly deserving of consideration.

author: David Leisering
title: Ozzie Albies homers twice, including walk-off, in Braves' win Saturday
desc: Ozzie Albies went 3-for-4 with three runs scored, two home runs, and three runs batted in on Saturday as he lifted the Braves to a 4-3 victory over the Brewers.
impact: Albies nearly single-handedly was Atlanta's offense on Saturday as he had three of the Braves' six hits, scored three of their four runs, and also drove in three in the victory. Albies put the first run of the game on the board in the bottom of the fifth with a solo home run off of Kyle Harrison. He, then, provided the heroics for the Braves in the ninth, sending an offering from Aaron Ashby over the right field wall - just inside the pole - with one on and one out for the walk-off winner. Albies is hitting .327 (18-for-55) with three homers and 11 RBI in 15 games this month. After a bit of a down season last year, Albies has rebounded in 2026 and is hitting .284 with 12 home runs and 40 RBI in 75 games this season.

author: David Leisering
title: Chris Sale allows two unearned runs in no-decision Saturday
desc: Chris Sale was charged with two runs - both unearned - on five hits in 5.2 innings on Saturday in a no-decision against the Brewers.
impact: Sale walked one and struck out seven, but needed 101 pitches to get through 5.2 innings on Saturday. It was the eighth time in 14 starts this season he has thrown at least 100 pitches in a game. He settled for a no-decision and has not won a game since May 28 against the Red Sox. In his three June starts, Sale is 0-2 with a 2.65 ERA while posting a 19:4 K:BB ratio in 17 innings. He has, however, failed to get through six innings in each of his last four starts. But, the lefty is having another sensational year in Atlanta as he is 8-5 with a 2.14 ERA and a 99:21 K:BB ratio in 84 innings. Sale, who ranks fourth in the National League in ERA and fifth in strikeouts, is lined up for a road start in San Francisco on Friday his next time out.

author: David Leisering
title: Colin Rea settles for no-decision Saturday
desc: Colin Rea went 5.1 scoreless innings on Saturday, allowing only three hits while striking out three in a no-decision against the Blue Jays.
impact: Rea, arguably, had his best start of the season on Saturday and exited with the Cubs holding a 3-0 lead. However, the bullpen imploded, allowing eight runs in the seventh and eighth innings to cost Rea a victory. It was his first scoreless outing of the season and the three hits he allowed were his fewest since giving up two hits in his first start of the year on April 8 against Cleveland. Rea is 5-5 with a 4.99 ERA and a 59:28 K:BB ratio through 16 appearances (12 starts). He's lined up for a start against the Mets in his next time out on Thursday.

author: David Leisering
title: Pete Crow-Armstrong remains scorching hot, homers again Saturday
desc: Pete Crow-Armstrong went 2-for-4 with a two-run home run on Saturday in the Cubs' 8-6 loss to the Blue Jays.
impact: Crow-Armstrong took Lazaro Estrada deep with two outs in the bottom of the sixth which, at the time, extended the Cubs' lead to 5-0. He also singled and walked, reaching base three times in the loss. Crow-Armstrong is putting up video game numbers at the moment as he is hitting a ridiculous .552 (16-for-29) with five homers, eight RBI, and three stolen bases in his last seven games. For the month of June, he is batting .437 (31-for-71) with four doubles, two triples, nine home runs, 14 RBI, and six stolen bases across 17 games. He's now tied for third in the National League with 18 steals, fifth with 83 hits, and tied for eighth with 16 home runs through 77 games this season.
